{{Short description|Subset of the natural numbers in set theory}}
{{More footnotes|date=June 2014}}
In [[set theory]], '''0<sup>†</sup>''' ('''zero [[†|dagger]]''') is a particular subset of the natural numbers,  first defined by [[Robert M. Solovay]] in unpublished work in the 1960s.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1=Kanamori | first1=Akihiro | author1-link=Akihiro Kanamori | last2=Awerbuch-Friedlander | first2=Tamara | author2-link = Tamara Awerbuch-Friedlander| title=The compleat 0<sup>†</sup> | doi=10.1002/malq.19900360206 |mr=1068949 | year=1990 | journal=Zeitschrift für Mathematische Logik und Grundlagen der Mathematik | issn=0044-3050 | volume=36 | issue=2 | pages=133–141}}</ref> The definition is a bit awkward, because there might be ''no'' set of natural numbers satisfying the conditions. Specifically, if [[ZFC]] is [[consistency|consistent]], then ZFC + "0<sup>†</sup> does not exist" is consistent. ZFC + "0<sup>†</sup> exists" is not known to be inconsistent (and most set theorists believe that it is consistent). In other words, it is believed to be independent (see [[Large cardinal property|large cardinal]] for a discussion). It is usually formulated as follows:

:0<sup>†</sup> exists [[if and only if]] there exists a non-trivial [[elementary embedding]] &nbsp;''j'' : ''L''[''U''] → ''L''[''U''] for the relativized [[Gödel constructible universe]] ''L''[''U''], where ''U'' is an [[ultrafilter]] witnessing that some [[cardinal number|cardinal]] ''κ'' is [[measurable cardinal|measurable]].

If 0<sup>†</sup> exists, then a careful analysis of the embeddings of ''L''[''U''] into itself reveals that there is a [[club set|closed unbounded subset]] of ''κ'', and a closed unbounded [[proper class]] of [[ordinal number|ordinal]]s greater than ''κ'', which together are ''[[indiscernibles|indiscernible]]'' for the structure (''L'', ∈, ''U''), and 0<sup>†</sup> is defined to be the set of [[Gödel number]]s of the true formulas about the indiscernibles in ''L''[''U''].

Solovay showed that the existence of 0<sup>†</sup> follows from the existence of two measurable cardinals. It is traditionally considered a [[large cardinal axiom]], although it is not even a cardinal, let alone a large one.

== See also ==

*[[Zero sharp|0<sup>#</sup>]]: a set of formulas (or subset of the integers) defined in a similar fashion, but  simpler.
